newsitem.title: USA: USDA outlines assistance to Fran victims.
newsitem.headline: USDA outlines assistance to Fran victims.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday his department had dispatched several emergency response teams to help the Federal Emergency Management Agency and local officials in the aftermath of Hurricane Fran.
Local governments have USDA food stocks on hand and they can begin using that food right away, Glickman said in a statement.
USDA's Food and Consumer Service is working with state agencies and voluntary relief groups like the American Red Cross to provide food supplies to evacuees, he said.
FCS may also distribute food directly to households in cases where the retail food distribution system is disrupted, Glickman said.
USDA's Forest Service has sent an emergency action team to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, to coordinate receiving and delivery of generators, water, cots, plastic tarps and other materials.
The statement also said USDA's Farm Service Agency can make low-interest loans to family farmers in disaster areas to help them recover from production or physical losses.

Reports from the area indicate that most of the peanut crop is still in the fields, as is one-third of the burley tobacco crop. Corn, soybean and sweet potato crops are also vulnerable to wind and water damage, Glickman said.
Cattle producers in counties that suffer a 40-percent or greater loss in feed production are eligible for cost-share assistance under the Disaster Reserve Assistance Program, he said.
And, the Non-insured Crop Disaster Assistance Program was available to farmers growing crops for which federal crop insurance is currently unavailable, he said.
